digest.component_or_area: dependency advisory gating and CI lane strategy
propositions: A committed lock freezes transitive dependencies, causing any published advisory on a pinned version to block CI for all in-flight changes regardless of whether those changes touched the dependency map.
The current pip-audit gate is non-discriminating: it blocks Gerrit verify changes that do not touch dependency declarations, punishing authors for advisories they did not cause and cannot fix.

The remediation ladder (upgrade direct dependency → override upstream cap → track upstream fix) was not widely known; developers independently reached for constraint-dependencies (which can only narrow and returns UNSATISFIABLE as expected output) and false-concluded that upgrades were impossible.

The retry logic in the pip-audit job only retries DB-UNREACHABLE failures, making 'recheck' everyone's first instinct despite it being unable to clear real findings, a time-wasting property that must be documented.

A mechanism is needed to notice when an override-dependencies suppression has become stale (its REMOVE-WHEN condition met), either periodic or triggered, to prevent overrides from becoming permanent by default.
